title: whoami
definition: A command that prints the effective username of the currently logged-in user.
simpleExplanation: Looking at your own nametag. It tells you exactly who the computer thinks you are right now.
realWorldExample: You SSH into a massive corporate server. You aren't sure if you logged in as yourself or as the admin. You type `whoami` and it prints `root`. You immediately become very careful.
useCases: Scripting conditions (e.g., abort if not root)

basic: What will `whoami` output if you run it like this: `sudo whoami`?
intermediate: What is the difference between the `whoami` command and the `who` command?

answers.question: Output of sudo whoami?
answers.answer: It will output `root`, because `sudo` temporarily changes your effective user ID to the superuser.

answers.question: whoami vs who?
answers.answer: `whoami` only prints your own username. `who` prints a list of EVERY user currently logged into the entire server, including where they logged in from.
